rounds.text: Amal Ltd demonstrates exceptional intrinsic value supported by a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 985 per share against a market price of Rs 758, leaving a healthy margin of safety of 23.1% [E42, E43]. The company exhibits elite operational efficiency, delivering a robust ROCE of 26.0% and an ROE of 20.4%, alongside a rules-based screen score of 90 out of 100 with medium confidence [E12, E13, E60]. Growth metrics are equally impressive, highlighted by a 58% compounded sales growth over 3 years and a massive 78% growth over the trailing twelve months [E15, E16]. Balance sheet health is pristine as the company is almost debt free with a debt-to-equity ratio of -0.00x and comfortable short-term liquidity backed by a current ratio of 2.48x [E35, E36, E56]. Furthermore, the business benefits from a supportive macroeconomic environment with the chemicals sector positioned in a clear tailwind with a score of +0.83 [E66, E68]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated price-to-book ratio of 7.78x and a TTM operating margin contraction of 4 percentage points [E2, E27].

Amal Ltd is fundamentally compounding at an exceptional rate, backed by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 51% [E14] and a TTM sales growth reaching 78% [E16], drastically outpacing the sector median sales growth of 17.9% [E70]. The underlying profitability is robust and efficient, demonstrated by a 26.0% ROCE [E12] and a 20.4% ROE [E13], which tower over respective sector benchmarks of 9.76% [E10] and 8.09% [E9]. The company is virtually debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of -0.00x [E35], complete short-term liquidity through a 2.48x current ratio [E36], and full cash backing of profits shown by a 1.00x cash conversion [E31]. Valuation models detect a significant mispricing, as a discounted cash flow analysis places intrinsic value at Rs 985 against the current market price of Rs 758 [E42], offering a clear 23.1% margin of safety [E43]. Furthermore, rules-based screens rate the stock a strong 90 out of 100 on the back of monumental year-on-year sales and net profit spikes [E60, E61, E63], operating inside a chemicals sector experiencing a powerful macro tailwind of +0.83 [E68]. Conceded: [E6].

Conceded: [E14], [E16], [E70], [E12], [E13], [E10], [E9], [E35], [E36], [E31], [E42], [E43], [E60], [E61], [E63], [E68]. While the bull highlights rapid top-line growth and high returns on capital, it glosses over the severe deterioration in recent profitability metrics, such as a -22% drop in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E19]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on high trailing returns overlooks the deeply inconsistent quarterly and yearly operating-margin trends [E29, E30], including a drop in operating margin from 18% three years ago to 14% in the TTM [E27] and a sharp decline from 25% down to 18% in the June 2026 quarter [E28]. The valuation multiples are stretched far beyond sector norms, with a price-to-book ratio of 7.77x against a sector benchmark of 1.89x [E7] and an EV/EBITDA of 18.68x versus a sector benchmark of 12.08x [E11]. This expensive pricing leaves little room for error, especially for a cyclical asset [E55] that has suffered a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -84.9% [E50] and an annualized volatility of 71.8% [E51].

Conceded: [E19], [E27], [E28], [E29], [E30]. The bear overstates valuation risk by ignoring that intrinsic value sits at Rs 985 per share against a market price of Rs 758, providing a genuine 23.1% margin of safety [E42, E43]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF demonstrates that today's price requires only a modest 14.4% earnings growth, which is safely below the 18.0% base case assumption [E44]. While volatility and historical drawdowns are cited [E50, E51], the company is fundamentally sound with a clean balance sheet, showing debt-to-equity at -0.00x, complete repayment of borrowings, and a cash surplus generated [E35, E56, E75]. Finally, the broader macroeconomic setting strongly supports the thesis, with the chemicals sector operating in a clear tailwind with a score of +0.83 [E66, E68], complemented by a high rules-based screen score of 90 out of 100 [E60].

The bull leans heavily on the discounted cash flow model pointing to a fair value of Rs 985 and a margin of safety [E42, E43], but this valuation optimism ignores severe underlying deterioration highlighted by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of -22% [E19]. Conceded: [E60]. While the reverse DCF implies a 14.4% growth rate requirement [E44], this metric conflicts with compressed operating margins that dropped to 14% in the TTM from 18% three years prior, alongside a sharp quarterly drop to 18% in June 2026 from 25% a year earlier [E27, E28]. Furthermore, the bull's emphasis on balance sheet strength [E35, E56, E75] bypasses the reality of high valuation multiples, including a price-to-book ratio of 7.78x and an EV/EBITDA of 18.68x that both trade well above sector benchmarks [E7, E11, E59]. Finally, pointing to sector tailwinds [E66, E68] does not neutralize the extreme annualised volatility of 71.8% and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -84.9% [E50, E51].
